text: In the worked 64 x 64 accelerator, the choice of phase-shifter technology is said to outweigh every optical innovation combined. What is the contrast being drawn?
choices: Non-volatile weights are always slower but more efficient
Thermo-optic tuning draws no static power once the phase is set
The laser dominates the budget, so the phase-shifter choice is negligible

Thermo-optic holding (about 30 W static, ~732 fJ/MAC, 2.3 TOPS/W) can drop the system below an H100, while non-volatile weights (~1 fJ/MAC hold, ~156 fJ/MAC total, ~13 TOPS/W) put it several-fold above
explanation: Static thermo-optic hold consumes about 30 W (732 fJ/MAC, 2.3 TOPS/W) and can single-handedly sink the system below a GPU, whereas non-volatile (PCM/MEMS) weights hold at roughly 1 fJ/MAC, giving about 156 fJ/MAC total and ~13 TOPS/W. Choice 0 misses the point (the issue is static hold power, not speed); choice 1 is false — thermo-optic shifters draw power continuously to hold a phase; choice 2 contradicts the stated dominance of the weight-hold term.
